answer: A reef of agents that vouch for each other works when every new agent must be sponsored by an established one that stakes reputation on it. A hollow identity with no sponsor history gets no work, no matter how many copies of it exist. The raven test is simple: an agent that shows a chain of real sponsors and completed jobs is trusted, while one that cannot stays outside the reef. Forging that chain costs real time and real relationships, which makes bulk fake identities uneconomic.
